rounds.fact: WordPress launched in 2003 as a small blogging tool and eventually grew to power a huge share of all websites on the internet, blogs and full businesses alike.
Hotmail was one of the first free webmail services, launched in 1996, and grew largely because every outgoing email carried a tagline advertising the service itself.
Ticketmaster moved a huge chunk of its ticket sales online in the late 90s, a shift that eventually made its service fees a much more visible (and criticized) part of buying tickets.
Gizmodo's early scoops on unreleased Apple products, sometimes from leaked prototypes, made it one of the most closely watched (and occasionally legally threatened) tech blogs of the 2000s.
ICQ (a pun on 'I seek you') launched in 1996 and is widely credited as the first mass-market instant messaging program, complete with its now-iconic 'uh-oh' message sound.
